title: A line through the scatter
question: How can a line fitted to scattered data predict what we have not measured?
hook: Scattered points never fall exactly on a line, yet a fitted line can still tell you something about the next one.
idea: Linear regression fits a straight-line relationship to known data, so the response can be predicted from new values and each coefficient read as a change per unit.

beats.prompt: A fitted model links sales to advertising spend. A new advertising budget arrives, but there are no sales figures for it yet. What can be done?

choices.label: Nothing, because the model needs an observed response first
choices.feedback: It is tempting to wait for data, but the fitted model already encodes the relationship.

choices.label: Use the fitted model to predict the sales response
Refit the model after throwing away the old data
choices.feedback: Old data are exactly what the model was fitted to; discarding them removes the relationship.

beats.explain: After a model is fitted, additional values of the explanatory variables collected without a response can be used to predict the response.

beats.prompt: Sort each description into the model it fits.
items: A single scalar predictor x and a single scalar response y
Several or vector-valued predictors, written with a capital X
beats.explain: The number of explanatory variables separates the two: one for simple regression, more for multiple regression.

beats.prompt: Match each term to what it is about.
pairs: A common way to fit a linear regression
Fitting by minimizing lack of fit in another norm
The model may fit the outliers more than the true data
beats.explain: Linear regression models are often fitted by least squares, but other fitting criteria exist, and nonlinear regression generalizes the idea.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: A model predicts y from two predictors, x1 and x2.
The fitted coefficient of x1 is 3.
So y is expected to rise by 3 for each one-unit rise in x1 with x2 held fixed.
So x1 on its own, ignoring x2, must also raise y by exactly 3.
beats.explain: A coefficient gives the unique effect with other predictors held fixed. The marginal effect of x1 on its own can be quite different, even nearly zero while the unique effect is large.
